user_impact: Default installs could not use release verification successfully unless signing was enabled, making the verifier look broken.
acceptance_criteria: Given a default unsigned release, `quickd releases verify --site demo` returns ok true; given deploy.signing.required true and an unsigned release, verify fails with an unsigned-manifest error; given a signed release that is tampered, verify fails.

user_story: As a site viewer, I want a site-authored `404.html` to appear for missing static routes so I get useful recovery links instead of a generic server page.
expected_behavior_from_code: When a release contains `404.html` and no SPA fallback handles the missing path, quickd serves that file with HTTP 404 for GET and HEAD, preserves hardening, and does not expose dotfiles or symlink escapes.
source_evidence: Gap audit against existing covered row HTTP-STATIC-005 and current product UX; not a restatement of existing row.
test_approach: Acceptance criteria in `acceptance_criteria` must be exercised by focused unit/integration/CLI/TUI tests and, where applicable, smoke tests.
notes: Implemented in `server/internal/static/static.go`; covered by `TestCustom404PageAndDirectoryListingOrder`; focused static tests pass. | Validation after this continuation: `cd server && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -count=1 ./...`, `zig build test`, `zig build terminal-test`, `cd sdk/js && bun test && bun run build`, and `just test-all` passed.
user_impact: A missing route shows a generic server 404 instead of the site-authored missing page, hurting navigation and trust.
acceptance_criteria: Given a site release with `404.html`, when I request `/missing`, then the response status is 404 and the body is the custom page; when I send HEAD, then status is 404 and the body is empty; when a SPA fallback is configured, SPA fallback still takes precedence.

user_story: As a viewer browsing a directory listing, I want directories and files sorted predictably so I can find content without guessing filesystem order.
expected_behavior_from_code: Directory listings sort directories before files and sort names case-insensitively within each group while still hiding dotfiles and symlink escapes.
source_evidence: Gap audit against existing covered row HTTP-STATIC-007 and current product UX; not a restatement of existing row.
test_approach: Acceptance criteria in `acceptance_criteria` must be exercised by focused unit/integration/CLI/TUI tests and, where applicable, smoke tests.
notes: Implemented in `server/internal/static/static.go`; covered by `TestCustom404PageAndDirectoryListingOrder`; focused static tests pass. | Validation after this continuation: `cd server && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -count=1 ./...`, `zig build test`, `zig build terminal-test`, `cd sdk/js && bun test && bun run build`, and `just test-all` passed.
user_impact: Unsorted filesystem order makes directory listings feel random and hard to scan as files grow.
acceptance_criteria: Given a directory with `a-dir/`, `z-dir/`, `A.txt`, `readme.txt`, and `z.txt`, the rendered listing appears in that order and excludes hidden files.

user_story: As browser code, I want `HEAD /_quick/uploads/:id` to check an upload without downloading the body.
expected_behavior_from_code: The uploads handler accepts HEAD for existing upload IDs, returns the same safe headers as GET, returns no body, and keeps authentication/site scoping unchanged.
source_evidence: Gap audit against existing covered row API-005 and current product UX; not a restatement of existing row.
test_approach: Acceptance criteria in `acceptance_criteria` must be exercised by focused unit/integration/CLI/TUI tests and, where applicable, smoke tests.
notes: Implemented in `server/internal/api/handler.go`; covered by `TestUploadHeadChecksStoredObject`; focused API tests pass. | Validation after this continuation: `cd server && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -count=1 ./...`, `zig build test`, `zig build terminal-test`, `cd sdk/js && bun test && bun run build`, and `just test-all` passed.
user_role: Browser app checking an uploaded file
user_impact: Apps must download a file just to confirm it exists or inspect metadata, wasting bandwidth.
acceptance_criteria: Given an uploaded text file, when a same-site authenticated caller sends HEAD to its upload URL, then the response is 200, has text/plain content type, and contains no body; missing IDs still return not found.

user_story: As an operator, I want a command to show the resolved config/profile/target with source precedence so I can confirm where commands will run before mutating anything.
expected_behavior_from_code: `quick config show --json` or equivalent prints config file path, active profile, site, remote, root, domain/base URL, and source for each resolved value without exposing secrets.
source_evidence: Added `quick config show` command in `src/cli/commands.c` and `src/cli/commands_openquick.c`; updated `opencli.json`, `README.md`, and `docs/design/WORKFLOW.md`.
test_approach: CLI contract covers help and `quick config show --json --profile lab --site lunch-vote --subdomain lunch-vote` with env-sourced remote/domain; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented resolved config/profile/target introspection with JSON/human output, config path, site/profile/subdomain/remote/root/domain/base URL/URL/IAP, and source-precedence metadata. Validated via OpenCLI contract and CLI tests.
user_impact: Users cannot easily tell which profile, config file, env var, or quick.json value won, causing deploys to target the wrong host.
acceptance_criteria: With flags, env vars, quick.json, and profile config set, the command reports the final value and source for each deploy-relevant field; secrets are redacted; exit is nonzero for invalid config.

user_story: As a site creator with an existing static folder, I want init to show conflicts and support a deliberate adopt/force flow so OpenQuick metadata can be added safely.
expected_behavior_from_code: Init detects existing files, lists exact conflicts, writes only missing metadata in adopt mode, and requires an explicit flag before overwriting generated files.
source_evidence: Added `quick init --adopt`, conflict preflight in `src/cli/commands_init.c`, core adopt-safe writing in `src/core/ops.{h,c}`, and updated `opencli.json`.
test_approach: CLI contract verifies re-init reports exact conflicts and `--adopt`, then `quick init --adopt` succeeds without overwriting existing files; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented safe init conflict detection and adopt mode: normal init refuses existing scaffold paths before writing anything and lists conflicts; adopt mode writes only missing OpenQuick metadata.
user_role: Site creator importing an existing static folder
user_impact: Users with existing HTML folders cannot safely adopt OpenQuick without guessing what will be overwritten.
acceptance_criteria: Given a folder with index.html, `quick init` reports the conflict and does not overwrite it; `quick init --adopt` writes quick.json/AGENTS/docs without changing index.html; `--force` overwrites only documented generated files.

user_story: As a first-time creator, I want to list available templates and preview their purpose before choosing one.
expected_behavior_from_code: `quick init --template list` or `quick templates` prints template names, descriptions, generated files, and whether SDK APIs are demonstrated.
source_evidence: Implemented `quick templates` and `quick init --template list` in `src/cli/commands_init.c`; registered command/options in `src/cli/commands.c`, updated `opencli.json`, README, and workflow docs.
test_approach: CLI contract verifies template list includes blank/realtime and sdk_demo metadata, and invalid `--template realtim` suggests realtime plus list commands; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented template discovery and invalid-template suggestions with names, descriptions, generated files, and SDK demo flags in human/JSON modes.
user_impact: Users must know template names in advance and cannot discover bundled examples from the CLI.
acceptance_criteria: The list includes blank and realtime; invalid template errors suggest the closest valid template and how to list them.

user_story: As a new user, I want init output and generated docs to guide me to local preview and host setup when no profile exists.
expected_behavior_from_code: If no default profile exists, init output includes `quick serve --dev`, `quick serve install`, and `quick deploy --dry-run` next steps; generated AGENTS/docs explain unbound state.
source_evidence: Updated init CLI output in `src/cli/commands_init.c` and scaffold agent guide in `src/core/ops.c`.
test_approach: CLI contract verifies first-run init output includes `quick serve --dev`, `quick serve install --profile`, and `quick deploy --dry-run`; scaffold docs include the same guidance; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented first-run onboarding: unbound init output points to local dev preview, host install, and dry-run deploy; generated AGENTS.md includes the local preview and host install loop. JSON includes first_run_guidance.
user_impact: After scaffolding, unbound users may not know how to preview locally or create a host profile.
acceptance_criteria: With isolated empty config, `quick init demo --plain` prints local preview and host setup next steps; with a default profile, it still prints deploy next steps without noise.

user_story: As a deployer, I want to roll a site back to the previous or selected release so I can recover quickly after publishing a broken site.
expected_behavior_from_code: CLI and quickd expose rollback that lists candidate releases, requires confirmation for mutation, swaps current atomically, records audit, and reports the restored URL/release.
test_approach: Regression tests: `TestRollbackSwitchesCurrentAndRecordsAudit`; CLI contract fake-SSH rollback confirmation/json path; full `zig build test`.
notes: Implemented rollback command for quickd and quick CLI: defaults to previous release or `--to <release>`, requires CLI typed confirmation unless `--yes`, atomically swaps current/previous, verifies target release, records rollback audit as `rollback:<deployer>`, updates OpenCLI contract/docs. Validated by deploy package tests and `zig build test`.
parent_feature: folder deploy via SSH and rsync
user_impact: A bad deploy cannot be reverted with the product, leaving users to manually edit symlinks on the host.
acceptance_criteria: Given two releases, `quick rollback SITE --to RELEASE --yes --json` makes current point at RELEASE, preserves the replaced release as previous, records deployer/audit metadata, and the site serves the old content.

user_story: As a deployer, I want cancelled or failed deploys to clean up staging or clearly tell me what remains.
expected_behavior_from_code: On cancellation/failure after prepare, the CLI asks quickd to remove incoming staging when safe, and reports cleanup success/failure.
source_evidence: Implemented `quickd deploy cleanup`/`Service.CleanupIncoming` plus CLI deploy cleanup attempts after prepared-staging failures/cancellations in `src/core/ops.c` and failure reporting in `src/cli/commands_deploy.c`.
test_approach: Service test verifies cleanup removes prepared `.incoming/<deploy_id>`; CLI contract simulates rsync transfer failure after prepare and verifies cleanup command succeeds and output reports cleaned staging; focused Go tests and `zig build test` pass.
notes: Implemented remote staging cleanup after prepare when overwrite confirmation aborts, cancellation occurs before/after transfer, transfer/extract fails, or activation fails. Cleanup failure messages include remaining staging path and exact cleanup command.
parent_feature: folder deploy via SSH and rsync
user_impact: Cancelled deploys can leave incoming staging directories that confuse operators or waste disk.
acceptance_criteria: Simulate cancellation after prepare: staging is removed or output includes the exact cleanup command/path; a later deploy is unaffected.

user_story: As a deployer, I want dry-run to summarize files added, changed, deleted, excluded, and total bytes so I can review before publishing.
expected_behavior_from_code: Dry-run produces a bounded human summary and full JSON detail from rsync dry-run/planning without activating a release.
source_evidence: Implemented dry-run transfer diff summary in `src/cli/commands_deploy.c`, persisted successful deploy manifests under `.quick/deployments/<profile>.manifest`, and documented behavior in README/workflow docs.
test_approach: CLI contract creates a prior manifest plus new/changed/deleted/excluded paths; JSON dry-run asserts added/changed/deleted/excluded arrays, and human dry-run asserts destructive delete warning; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented local transfer diff summary for dry-run: added, changed, deleted, and excluded path categories; human output highlights destructive deletes and JSON exposes category arrays/counts for automation.
user_impact: Dry-run output says what command would run but not which files/delete/size changes matter.
acceptance_criteria: For a site with one new file, one changed file, one excluded .env, and one deletion, dry-run JSON reports each category and the human output calls out destructive deletes.

user_story: As a deployer, I want transient prepare/transfer/activate failures to include retry guidance and safe retry behavior.
expected_behavior_from_code: Deploy distinguishes transient connection failures from validation failures, preserves idempotent safety, and suggests retry or cleanup.
source_evidence: Implemented CLI transient transfer failure guidance in `src/cli/commands_deploy.c`, with transfer phase reporting, cleanup status, and retry guidance; core cleanup was already in deploy failure path.
test_approach: CLI contract fake rsync exits with `network down`; assertions cover stderr containing network error, `phase transfer`, cleanup success, and `rerun quick deploy`; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented actionable retry output for transient transfer failures: failed phase, cleanup result, and clear rerun guidance when staging was cleaned.
parent_feature: folder deploy via SSH and rsync
user_impact: A transient SSH/rsync failure forces the user to restart without guidance.
acceptance_criteria: When rsync exits with a network error, output identifies transfer phase, says whether staging was cleaned, and a second deploy can succeed without manual host repair.

user_story: As a local developer, I want `quick serve --dev` to explain port conflicts and suggest another port.
expected_behavior_from_code: Port bind failures detect address-in-use, mention the occupied port, and suggest `--port` with a free candidate; JSON includes error code `port_in_use`.
source_evidence: Implemented listen error handling in `server/cmd/quickd/main.go` for dev server bind failures.
test_approach: Regression test `TestServeDevPortInUseSuggestsRecovery` reserves a loopback port and verifies the error names address-in-use and suggests `quick serve --dev --port`; focused Go test passes.
notes: Implemented friendly port-in-use recovery for quickd dev serving: pre-listens to detect EADDRINUSE, reports occupied port, and suggests a free `quick serve --dev --port` alternative plus direct quickd --listen form.
user_impact: If the dev port is occupied, users get a low-level bind error rather than a next action.
acceptance_criteria: Start a listener on 9366, run serve dev, and assert the error names port 9366 and suggests a replacement.

user_story: As an operator with many sites, I want list to sort/filter/search by name, profile, public flag, stale state, and deployer.
expected_behavior_from_code: `quick list` supports stable sort and filters in human and JSON modes without changing default output shape unexpectedly.
source_evidence: Implemented list view filtering/sorting in `src/cli/commands_list.c`, added `--filter`/`--sort` command metadata in `src/cli/commands.c`, regenerated `opencli.json`, and updated README/workflow docs.
test_approach: CLI contract fake remote returns mixed rows; `quick list --remote --filter demo --sort updated --json` asserts filter metadata and excludes non-matching zeta row; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented deterministic list filtering and sorting across parsed local/remote rows; JSON now includes filter query, sort key, total, and matched counts.
user_impact: Large host lists become hard to scan and scripts must do extra filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Given mixed local/remote rows, filters return only matching rows, sort order is deterministic, and JSON includes applied filter metadata.

feature: remote error state alongside local data
user_story: As an operator, I want list to show local data plus a clear remote-error state when the host cannot be reached.
expected_behavior_from_code: Remote failures set remote_ok false, include phase/error/remediation in JSON, and mark local rows stale in human output.
source_evidence: Added remote error fields to `quick_list_result_t`/`quick_op_list` and emitted `remote_ok`, `remote_requested`, and `remote_error` in `src/cli/commands_list.c`.
test_approach: CLI contract fake-SSH test verifies `quick list --remote --json` exits successfully with local/empty data plus `remote_ok:false`, `remote_error`, and `sites`; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented non-fatal remote list failures with phase/error/remediation metadata; JSON preserves local/empty site data and human output prints stale/remediation details.
user_role: Operator checking host state while offline
user_impact: When remote listing fails, users need to know local rows may be stale instead of seeing silence or partial truth.
acceptance_criteria: With fake ssh failure, list exits according to documented policy and JSON includes remote_requested true, remote_ok false, error detail, and any local rows marked stale.

user_story: As an operator, I want a short recovery window or explicit archive for deleted sites so accidental deletion can be reversed.
expected_behavior_from_code: Delete moves site data to a time-limited trash/archive or emits a restorable backup path, and a restore command can recover it before purge.
source_evidence: Implemented delete archive/restore in `server/internal/deploy/deploy.go`, `quickd sites restore|purge`, top-level `quick restore`, OpenCLI contract, README, and workflow docs.
test_approach: Deploy service test deletes to archive, restores current release/catalog, and purges an archive; CLI contract verifies delete JSON includes archive and `quick restore --from ... --yes --json` restores; focused Go tests and `zig build test` pass.
notes: Implemented recovery for mistaken deletes: delete moves site/uploads into `.trash/sites/<site>-<timestamp>`, reports archive path and restore command, `quick restore`/`quickd sites restore` restores files and catalog, and quickd purge permanently removes an archive.
user_impact: Typed confirmation reduces accidents but does not help after a mistaken deletion.
acceptance_criteria: After `quick delete demo --yes`, `quick restore demo --from <archive>` restores current release/catalog; purge permanently removes the archive.

user_story: As an operator, I want public-static scan failures to list file paths and matched patterns so I can fix them safely.
expected_behavior_from_code: Public-on and public-site deploy failures include bounded scan findings in human/JSON output without leaking file contents.
source_evidence: Implemented with `scan.FormatFindings`, `deploy.validatePublicRelease`, and `quickd sites public` error path in `server/cmd/quickd/main.go`.
test_approach: Regression tests: `TestFormatFindings`, public deploy rejection assertion in deploy tests, and `TestSitesPublicReportsScanFindings`.
notes: Implemented actionable scan findings for public-static enable/deploy failures; errors include bounded `file matched pattern` details. Focused Go tests pass.
user_impact: Public enable/deploy rejection can say only that APIs are used, leaving users to hunt through files.
acceptance_criteria: Given a release with `fetch("/_quick/identity")`, `quick public SITE on --json` returns status/fail with findings including file and pattern; human output shows remediation.

user_story: As an operator, I want domain add/list to show DNS and TLS readiness so I know when the domain can be used.
expected_behavior_from_code: Domain commands optionally check DNS target, Caddy ask endpoint, and HTTPS reachability; JSON includes pending/ok/fail statuses.
source_evidence: Implemented domain readiness payloads in `server/cmd/quickd/main.go`; `quickd domains list` now returns each domain with DNS/TLS readiness and remediation. README/workflow docs updated.
test_approach: Go unit test injects DNS lookup success and failure into readiness assessment, asserting ok status for mapped host and fail/remediation for missing host; `cd server && go test -count=1 ./cmd/quickd` passes.
notes: Implemented host-side domain readiness metadata: DNS success returns ok with addresses; DNS failure returns fail with remediation and pending TLS.
user_impact: Adding a domain to the catalog does not tell the user whether DNS and TLS are ready.
acceptance_criteria: For a domain with no DNS, list shows pending/fail with remediation; for a mapped test host, status is ok.

user_story: As an interactive operator, I want a warning before leaving edited settings that have not been written.
expected_behavior_from_code: Profile and site config screens track dirty state, mark unsaved fields, and confirm before Back/Esc/Exit discards changes.
source_evidence: Implemented dirty profile tracking and unsaved-changes decision menu in `src/tui/tui_screen_config.c`; documented TUI behavior in README and workflow docs.
test_approach: Ghostty VT terminal scenario edits a profile ssh field, backs out, verifies `UNSAVED PROFILE CHANGES`, chooses cancel, verifies the edit remains, then discards; `zig build terminal-test` passes.
notes: Implemented unsaved profile warning with save/discard/cancel; cancel returns to the editor with the in-memory edit intact.
user_impact: Users can navigate away after editing in-memory settings without realizing changes were not written.
acceptance_criteria: Edit a profile field, press Back, and assert the TUI asks to save/discard/cancel; choosing cancel returns to the editor with the edit intact.

user_story: As an interactive deployer, I want cancelling a deploy to report whether remote staging was cleaned and what to do next.
expected_behavior_from_code: TUI cancel sets the deploy cancel flag, attempts safe cleanup if prepared, and shows cleanup result/remediation.
source_evidence: Implemented TUI deploy cancellation cleanup messaging in `src/tui/tui_screen_deploy.c`; mapped rsync 130/143 transfer exits to cancellation in `src/core/ops.c`; added terminal fake harness coverage and docs.
test_approach: Ghostty VT fake harness makes first rsync return 130 after prepare, asserts `DEPLOY CANCELLED` plus `remote staging cleaned`, then reruns deploy and asserts `DEPLOY COMPLETE`; `zig build terminal-test` passes.
notes: Implemented cancelled deploy modal with cleanup status/path. Transfer cancellation exits now trigger cleanup and a retry can deploy successfully in the TUI harness.
user_impact: The TUI can cancel progress but users need clear cleanup status and retry safety.
acceptance_criteria: Cancel during transfer in a fake harness; modal says cancelled, staging cleaned or exact path remains, and a follow-up deploy succeeds.

user_story: As a screen-reader user, I want every TUI action to have an equivalent plain CLI path advertised from the TUI/help.
expected_behavior_from_code: Help/About and screen footers list CLI equivalents for current actions; docs explain headless/no-TUI workflow.
source_evidence: Added CLI-equivalent command hints to TUI main menu descriptions and Help keybindings in `src/tui/tui_app.c`; README/workflow docs updated.
test_approach: Ghostty VT test asserts main menu exposes `CLI: quick list --remote` and Help includes `CLI equivalents`; `zig build terminal-test` passes.
notes: Implemented discoverable non-fullscreen fallback commands in TUI menu/help so workflows can be continued via CLI without mouse/color dependence.
user_impact: Full-screen terminal UI may be hard for screen readers even when CLI commands exist.
acceptance_criteria: In TUI help and each major screen, the user can discover the matching CLI command without using mouse or color.

user_story: As a host operator, I want quickd to list releases with current/previous markers, deployer, time, files, bytes, and verification status.
expected_behavior_from_code: `quickd releases list --site SITE --json` returns ordered release metadata and verification summaries; human output is stable.
source_evidence: Implemented `Service.ListReleases`, `store.DeploysForSite`, and `quickd releases list --site SITE --json` in `server/internal/deploy`, `server/internal/store`, and `server/cmd/quickd/main.go`.
test_approach: Regression tests: deploy rollback/history test checks current/previous/deployer/created_at/verification; quickd command test `TestReleasesListCommandReportsHistory`; focused Go tests pass.
notes: Implemented release history listing with ordered release records, current/previous markers, latest deployer/audit time per release, and verification status/summary.
user_impact: Verify can check releases but users cannot list release history without filesystem access.
acceptance_criteria: After three deploys, releases list marks current and previous, includes metadata from manifests/store, and supports selecting a release for rollback.

user_story: As a host operator, I want to export deploy/domain/public/admin audit events for review.
expected_behavior_from_code: An admin audit command streams JSONL/CSV with time, actor, action, site, release/domain, and source metadata.
source_evidence: Added `audit_events` storage, redacting `RecordAudit`/`ExportAudit`, mutation hooks for deploy/public/domain/delete in `server/internal/store/store.go`, and `quickd audit export --json` in `server/cmd/quickd/main.go`.
test_approach: Go test performs deploy, public, domain, and delete actions, exports audit JSON, asserts chronological actions and secret-like SSH key metadata redaction; `cd server && go test -count=1 ./cmd/quickd ./internal/store` passes.
notes: Implemented host audit export with chronological events and secret-like metadata redaction.
user_impact: Stats show recent deploys but not a complete exportable audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: After deploy/domain/public/delete actions, audit export contains each event in chronological order and redacts secrets.

user_story: As a viewer, I want precompressed `.br`/`.gz` assets to be served when my browser supports them.
expected_behavior_from_code: If `app.js.br` or `app.js.gz` exists and Accept-Encoding allows it, quickd serves it with Content-Encoding, correct Vary, and the original content type.
source_evidence: Implemented precompressed static asset negotiation in `server/internal/static/static.go` for `.br`/`.gz`, setting `Content-Encoding` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`; docs updated.
test_approach: Static handler test writes `app.js.br`, requests `Accept-Encoding: br, gzip`, asserts br body/header/Vary, then requests without encoding and asserts fallback to original; `cd server && go test -count=1 ./internal/static` passes.
notes: Implemented precompressed asset serving with brotli preferred over gzip and normal fallback when no accepted variant exists.
user_impact: Large static assets are sent uncompressed unless the edge handles them.
acceptance_criteria: Request `/app.js` with `Accept-Encoding: br`; response serves `/app.js.br`, sets `Content-Encoding: br`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, and falls back when absent.

user_story: As a viewer, I want site-branded or at least useful error pages for denied and unavailable content.
expected_behavior_from_code: 403/401/500 paths can use safe site error pages or a consistent OpenQuick page with recovery links, while preserving status codes.
source_evidence: Implemented friendly forbidden static error handling in `server/internal/static/static.go`, including optional site `403.html` and a generic no-leak OpenQuick fallback page with home recovery link; README documents `403.html`/`404.html`.
test_approach: `cd server && go test -count=1 ./internal/static` covers symlink escape returning 403 with fallback recovery link, custom site `403.html`, no leaked outside path, and existing custom 404 behavior.
notes: Implemented friendly 403 static pages while preserving status codes and avoiding filesystem path leakage.
user_impact: Forbidden/not found errors are plain server text and do not help viewers navigate back.
acceptance_criteria: Request a symlink escape and receive 403 with no leaked path details plus a recovery link or site 403 page.

user_story: As a viewer denied by identity policy, I want a clear permission-denied page or JSON error explaining the next step.
expected_behavior_from_code: Browser navigation receives a non-leaky HTML page for static/directory requests; API requests receive structured JSON with code and remediation.
source_evidence: Implemented friendly permission-denied renderer in `server/internal/static/static.go` for browser/static/directory requests while preserving JSON for `/_quick/*` APIs.
test_approach: Static handler test verifies non-loopback denied browser navigation gets a non-leaky HTML access page and API path gets structured JSON; focused static tests pass.
notes: Implemented friendly access-required HTML for navigation/directory denials and kept API denials JSON with original identity error.
user_impact: A raw unauthorized error does not tell users whether to sign in, switch accounts, or ask an admin.
acceptance_criteria: Anonymous/denied static request returns 401/403 with text/html recovery page; `/_quick/*` returns JSON `{error,code,remediation}` without trusting spoofed headers.

user_story: As browser code, I want paginated document lists so large collections load predictably.
expected_behavior_from_code: DB list accepts `limit` and cursor parameters, returns documents plus `next_cursor` and stable ordering, and enforces max limits.
source_evidence: Implemented DB pagination in `server/internal/store/store.go` and `server/internal/api/handler.go` with `limit`, `cursor`, stable created_at/id ordering, `next_cursor`, max limit clamp, and invalid-cursor 400 handling.
test_approach: API integration test paginates DB documents across limit/cursor pages and verifies bad cursors return 400; focused Go API/store tests pass.
notes: Implemented paginated document list endpoint with stable cursor-based ordering and bounded limit.
user_impact: Listing all documents does not scale and gives no end-of-list marker.
acceptance_criteria: With 101 docs and limit 50, first response has 50 docs and next_cursor, second has next 50, third has 1 and no next_cursor; invalid limits return 400.

user_story: As browser code, I want safe server-side filter and sort options for simple document fields.
expected_behavior_from_code: DB list supports a small documented query DSL with allowlisted operators, stable sort, per-site isolation, and injection-safe storage behavior.
source_evidence: Implemented DB list equality filtering and deterministic sort handling in `server/internal/api/handler.go`; README documents supported filter/sort keys.
test_approach: API integration test creates closed/open documents, requests `filter={"status":"open"}&sort=-created_at`, asserts only open documents in descending order, and verifies unsupported operator returns 400; `cd server && go test -count=1 ./internal/api` passes.
notes: Implemented top-level JSON equality filters and sort keys `created_at`, `updated_at`, `id` (with `-` descending); unsupported nested/operator filters are rejected.
user_impact: Apps must fetch every document to filter or sort client-side.
acceptance_criteria: Filter by status and sort by created_at returns only matching site documents in the requested order; unsupported operators return validation errors.

user_story: As browser code, I want revision/ETag preconditions for updates so users do not lose work.
expected_behavior_from_code: Documents include revision/updated_at tokens; PUT/PATCH/DELETE accept If-Match or revision and return 409 on stale writes.
source_evidence: Implemented document `revision`/ETag generation and If-Match/query revision precondition checks in `server/internal/api/handler.go`.
test_approach: API integration test verifies create returns revision/ETag, matching If-Match update succeeds, stale If-Match returns 409 `revision_mismatch`, and delete accepts current revision; focused API tests pass.
notes: Implemented optimistic concurrency for DB writes: documents expose revision, single-document responses set ETag, PATCH/PUT/DELETE honor If-Match or `revision` query, and stale writes return structured 409 conflict.
user_impact: Concurrent edits can overwrite each other without warning.
acceptance_criteria: Two clients read a doc; client A updates; client B update with old revision gets 409 and current revision in response.

user_story: As browser code, I want to list uploads with metadata so users can manage previously uploaded files.
expected_behavior_from_code: `GET /_quick/uploads` returns paginated upload metadata scoped to site and identity policy; SDK exposes `quick.uploads.list`.
source_evidence: Implemented upload listing in `server/internal/store/store.go` and `server/internal/api/handler.go`, persisted upload names, added SDK `quick.uploads.list`, rebuilt SDK and embedded copy, and updated README.
test_approach: API integration test uploads two files then lists `/ _quick/uploads` metadata; SDK test verifies `uploads.list({limit,cursor})` URL, array compatibility, and `next_cursor`; server API tests and Bun SDK tests pass.
notes: Implemented paginated upload list returning ids, names, sizes, content types, created_by, created_at, URLs, and SDK list metadata.
user_impact: Uploads can be created/read/deleted by ID but not listed for a site/user.
acceptance_criteria: After two uploads, list returns both IDs, names, sizes, content types, created_by, and supports pagination.

user_story: As a user uploading a large file through an OpenQuick app, I want progress and cancellation so I am not stuck waiting blindly.
expected_behavior_from_code: SDK upload accepts progress and AbortSignal; server treats aborted uploads as cleanup candidates and returns structured errors.
source_evidence: Implemented SDK upload progress stream and AbortSignal propagation in `sdk/js/src/index.ts`, rebuilt `sdk/js/dist/quick.js` and embedded `server/internal/api/sdk/quick.js`; README updated.
test_approach: SDK test uploads a Blob with `onProgress` and AbortSignal, fake fetch consumes the stream, asserts raw upload path, signal propagation, and final loaded/total progress; Bun SDK tests pass.
notes: Implemented progress/cancel client behavior: `quick.uploads.put` can stream raw upload bytes, report loaded/total progress, and propagate abort signals. Server continues to create upload records only after full body save succeeds.
user_impact: Large uploads provide no SDK progress, cancellation, or resume affordance.
acceptance_criteria: A mocked upload reports progress, abort cancels the request and no completed upload record remains.

user_story: As a collaborative app user, I want realtime subscriptions to reconnect with backoff after transient network drops.
expected_behavior_from_code: SDK keeps subscriptions, reconnects automatically with bounded exponential backoff, emits connection state, and avoids duplicate handlers.
source_evidence: Implemented SDK realtime reconnection/backoff state machine in `sdk/js/src/index.ts`; rebuilt `sdk/js/dist/quick.js` and embedded `server/internal/api/sdk/quick.js`.
test_approach: Bun test uses a fake WebSocket and fake timer to verify abnormal close emits disconnected/reconnecting/connected states, schedules bounded backoff, creates a new socket, resubscribes once, and delivers later events without duplicate callbacks.
notes: Implemented realtime reconnect/backoff: SDK keeps channel subscriptions, emits connection state through `quick.realtime.onStateChange`, reconnects with bounded exponential backoff, resubscribes on open, and avoids duplicate handlers.
user_impact: A dropped WebSocket silently stops updates until app code manually reconnects.
acceptance_criteria: When the socket closes abnormally, SDK emits disconnected/reconnecting/connected, resubscribes existing channels, and receives later events once reconnected.

user_story: As a browser user, I want to cancel a long AI response so I can change my prompt without waiting.
expected_behavior_from_code: SDK chat/image accept AbortSignal; server respects request context cancellation and does not record successful audit usage for cancelled calls.
source_evidence: SDK request layer now converts AbortError into typed `OpenQuickError` code `aborted` and preserves abort through AI capability and chat paths in `sdk/js/src/index.ts`; embedded SDK rebuilt.
test_approach: SDK test makes fetch throw AbortError during AI chat capability check and asserts rejected error is `OpenQuickError` with code `aborted`; Bun SDK tests pass. Server provider requests already use request contexts and provider timeouts.
notes: Implemented typed AI abort behavior; AbortSignal remains propagated through AI fetches and server provider calls use request context/timeouts.
user_impact: Long AI requests cannot be cancelled cleanly from SDK affordances.
acceptance_criteria: Abort a streaming chat request; fetch is cancelled, server provider request context is cancelled, and SDK throws a typed abort error.

user_story: As an AI-enabled site user, I want rate limit errors to include retry timing and quota context.
expected_behavior_from_code: AI rate limit responses use 429 with Retry-After and JSON code/scope/reset fields; SDK surfaces them as typed errors.
test_approach: Regression coverage in `TestAIStreamingAnthropicAndAnonymousRateLimits` verifies Retry-After plus JSON `code`, `scope`, and `reset` for rpm and daily budget failures; focused API tests pass.
notes: Implemented Retry-After and structured JSON rate-limit/quota metadata for AI rpm and daily-budget limits: code, scope, limit, reset, retry_after, and human error.
user_impact: Rate-limited users need to know when to retry instead of seeing a generic error.
acceptance_criteria: Exhaust per-identity rate limit; response is 429 with Retry-After and body includes code `rate_limited`, scope, and reset time.

user_story: As browser code, I want warehouse query metadata so I can render forms and tables safely.
expected_behavior_from_code: Capabilities or a warehouse metadata endpoint lists query names, params, max rows, and documented columns without exposing SQL.
source_evidence: Implemented `GET /_quick/warehouse` metadata in `server/internal/api/warehouse.go`, route support in handler, SDK `quick.warehouse.metadata`, rebuilt embedded SDK, and updated README.
test_approach: Warehouse API test asserts metadata includes query name, params/max_rows/columns and omits SQL/database strings; SDK test asserts metadata surface; server API and Bun SDK tests pass.
notes: Implemented warehouse query metadata without exposing SQL or database credentials; columns are derived with a zero-row query.
user_impact: Apps cannot discover query params/columns without out-of-band docs.
acceptance_criteria: Configured query metadata returns name/params/max_rows/columns and omits SQL/database credentials.

user_story: As a site author, I want SDK errors with status, code, response body, and retry info so I can show the right UI state.
expected_behavior_from_code: requestJson/requestChatStream throw OpenQuickError with status, code, details, retryAfter, and original cause where available.
source_evidence: Implemented typed SDK errors with exported `OpenQuickError` in `sdk/js/src/index.ts` and rebuilt `sdk/js/dist/quick.js` plus embedded `server/internal/api/sdk/quick.js`.
test_approach: Bun tests cover `OpenQuickError` status/code/details/retryAfter from JSON 429 responses; `bun run build`, `bun test`, and `just build-sdk` pass.
notes: Implemented typed OpenQuickError for non-OK requestJson and streaming responses, preserving status, code, parsed details, and Retry-After retry metadata.
user_impact: String-only errors force apps to parse text and cannot distinguish auth, validation, rate limit, or network failures.
acceptance_criteria: Mock 401/400/429/network failures and assert catch receives typed properties without parsing message text.

user_story: As a site author, I want SDK methods to accept AbortSignal so cancel buttons work across OpenQuick APIs.
expected_behavior_from_code: DB, uploads, AI, warehouse, and capabilities methods accept options with signal and pass it to fetch/WebSocket where applicable.
source_evidence: Added `RequestOptions`/`signal` support across DB, uploads, AI chat/image, warehouse query, and capabilities calls in `sdk/js/src/index.ts`; rebuilt dist and embedded SDK.
test_approach: Bun tests verify DB list passes AbortSignal through fetch; build and SDK tests pass.
notes: Implemented AbortSignal pass-through for SDK fetch-based request families and stream chat fetch; realtime WebSocket remains event-based.
user_impact: Users cannot cancel slow DB/upload/AI actions through SDK options consistently.
acceptance_criteria: A test aborts a pending DB list/upload/chat fetch and receives an AbortError/OpenQuickError marked aborted.

user_story: As a site author, I want `collection.list({limit,cursor,filter,sort})` so list views can page and search without hand-building URLs.
expected_behavior_from_code: SDK exposes list options and returns documents plus pagination metadata while preserving existing bare-array compatibility.
source_evidence: Updated `sdk/js/src/index.ts` DB list options/result types and rebuilt `sdk/js/dist/quick.js` plus embedded `server/internal/api/sdk/quick.js`.
test_approach: Bun tests verify list sends limit/cursor/filter/sort query options, preserves array compatibility, and exposes documents/next_cursor metadata; `bun run build`, `bun test`, and `just build-sdk` pass.
notes: Implemented SDK DB list options with query serialization and array-compatible pagination metadata (`documents`, `next_cursor`, `nextCursor`).
user_impact: SDK `list()` has no parameters for pagination/filter/sort even if the server gains them.
acceptance_criteria: Existing `list()` still returns an array; `listPage({limit:50})` or documented equivalent returns `{documents,nextCursor}`.

user_story: As a host operator, I want `quickd config check/explain` to validate config files and show defaults.
expected_behavior_from_code: Command validates unknown fields, safety gates, AI/warehouse config, derived defaults, and redacts env-secret values.
source_evidence: Implemented `quickd config check` and `quickd config explain` in `server/cmd/quickd/main.go`.
test_approach: Command test `TestConfigCheckAndExplain` validates JSON check/explain output, derived defaults, and secret redaction policy; focused quickd tests pass.
notes: Implemented quickd config validation/explain command using existing strict config loader/defaults, with JSON summary of effective settings/defaults and secret redaction guidance.
user_impact: Strict config is safe but operators need a way to validate and explain it before restarting the daemon.
acceptance_criteria: Given valid config, check exits 0 and prints normalized defaults; given typo field, exits nonzero with path to the field and remediation.

user_story: As a host operator, I want upgrade steps to back up config/data and roll back the binary if health checks fail.
expected_behavior_from_code: Install docs or command create timestamped backups, install new binary, run doctor/health, and restore old binary/config on failure.
source_evidence: Implemented `quick serve install --execute` remote backup and doctor-failure rollback in `src/cli/commands_serve.c`; README updated.
test_approach: CLI contract fake SSH/SCP simulates successful install steps and failing post-install `quickd doctor`; asserts backup path output, rollback messaging, and fake restore command invocation; `zig build test` passes.
notes: Implemented remote backup of quickd binary/config/systemd unit before execute install and automatic restore with reported backup path when post-install doctor fails.
user_impact: Install assets do not define an upgrade rollback procedure for quickd/config/data.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated failed post-install doctor leaves the previous quickd binary/config active and reports backup paths.

user_story: As a site creator, I want examples that demonstrate empty, loading, error, permission denied, rate limited, and offline states.
expected_behavior_from_code: Example sites include accessible UI state patterns and comments for each SDK family.
source_evidence: Added `examples/sites/states-demo/` with accessible loading, empty, error, permission-denied, rate-limited, and offline states; documented examples in README; added `scripts/validate-examples-states.py` and wired it into `just test-all`.
test_approach: Ran `scripts/validate-examples-states.py`; validator asserts required state containers, accessibility roles, OpenQuickError handling, unhandled rejection recovery, offline detection, and no console.error/throw-based failure pattern.
notes: Implemented robust UI states example and deterministic validation script.
user_impact: Examples show happy paths but not robust user-facing states.
acceptance_criteria: Running examples in dev shows visible empty/loading/error containers and no console errors when APIs fail.

user_story: As an AI agent, I want the OpenQuick deploy skill to force a pre-deploy safety checklist so risky deployments are not accidental.
expected_behavior_from_code: Skill instructs agents to check quick.json output, secrets, public_static/IAP status, overwrite confirmation, and post-deploy smoke before reporting success.
source_evidence: Added an Agent deploy safety checklist to `skills/openquick-deploy/SKILL.md`, refreshed rollback/restore/config/list command references, removed stale no-rollback guidance, and added build-time checklist assertions in `skills/build.sh`.
test_approach: Ran `skills/build.sh`; package build now fails if the skill omits the deploy safety checklist, dry-run requirement, or targeted doctor requirement.
notes: Implemented skill-level safety checklist requiring target confirmation, dry-run diff review, doctor, secret/public scan checks, overwrite approval, cleanup reporting, and rollback/restore capture.
user_impact: An agent can deploy without an explicit checklist for public/IAP/secrets/overwrite risks.
acceptance_criteria: Skill package contains checklist text and reference links; a packaging test verifies the skill includes the checklist.
